posts.title: 0.05 seconds
posts.notes: Check the latest reported 0 to 60 figure for the Roadster before posting. Reports differ, so the copy says "about half a second".
posts.caption:
0.05 seconds.

That is how long it takes to judge a web page. In a well-known study, people rated how appealing a page looked after seeing it for 50 milliseconds, and their snap judgments matched what they said after a longer look (Lindgaard, Fernandes, Dudek and Brown, 2006).

The new Tesla Roadster demo claims 0 to 60 mph in about half a second. That is ten times longer than your visitor needs to make up their mind about your site.

Before the copy, the animation or the clever idea, layout, type, colour and space do the first job. What does yours say in 50 ms?
posts.first_comment: Study: Lindgaard, Fernandes, Dudek and Brown (2006), Behaviour & Information Technology. oopsweb.co

posts.title: World Usability Day: five checks
posts.notes: Post on the day (Thu 12 Nov). The PDF is the swipeable version.
posts.caption:
Happy World Usability Day. Here are five checks you can run on your own site before your coffee gets cold.

1. Tap targets. WCAG 2.2 level AA asks for at least 24 px. Apple suggests 44, Material 48.
2. Contrast. Level AA asks for 4.5 to 1 on normal text.
3. Focus. Tab through your page. Can you see where you are?
4. Line length. 45 to 75 characters a line; typographers aim for about 66.
5. Error messages. Say what went wrong and how to fix it.

Then do the sixth check: watch one real person use it. It tells you more than a week of meetings.

posts.title: Elements 01: Button
posts.notes: Elements 01, a 12 s loop at 60 fps: the 9:16 reel goes to Instagram and YouTube, the 4:5 cut to LinkedIn and X. Sound is clicks and pops over our series track. Cover frame: the element mid-action, with the headline showing.
posts.caption:
Press it!

Elements 01: Button. A button should feel glad you pressed it.

It leans toward the cursor before you arrive, fills from the side you came from and goes down like a key. Then it tells you what happened: loading, then sent. Every state answers one question: did that work?

The values: Pulls 12% toward the cursor, fills from where you came in, squashes to 94% and springs back. Loading to sent in 1.4 s.

Elements is our new series: one interface element at a time, the small details that make a site feel alive. Happy accidents happen.

posts.title: Elements 03: Text field
posts.notes: Elements 03, a 12 s loop at 60 fps: the 9:16 reel goes to Instagram and YouTube, the 4:5 cut to LinkedIn and X. Sound is clicks and pops over our series track. Cover frame: the element mid-action, with the headline showing.
posts.caption:
Type it!

Elements 03: Text field. Happy World Usability Day. Most forms lose people at the moment they type.

The label floats out of the way, each letter lands, and a wrong email gets a small shake and a sentence that says how to fix it. Fix it, and a check draws in. No red wall of errors, no guessing.

The values: Keys land every 6 frames, give or take 2. A bad address shakes 18 px (damped in 0.17 s); the eye morphs 10 dots in 0.5 s.

Elements is our new series: one interface element at a time, the small details that make a site feel alive. Happy accidents happen.
